subject: Next steps: VPC residency risk map + prioritized asks
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Desai <maya.desai@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: VPC residency risk map + prioritized asks

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Key pain points / drivers you shared:
- PHI processing for certain datasets must remain within Novamed-controlled infrastructure (air-gapped for those flows).
- Strict egress controls: only limited outbound channels allowed (SFTP to partner buckets, approved vendor IPs).
- Regulatory map: HIPAA + EU data residency requirements for a subset of patient data.

Goals we heard:
- Pilot an on-prem/VPC-hosted inference path for triage workflows by Q1 2028.
- Maintain <150ms p95 inference latency for prioritized endpoints.
- Clear evidence for SOC2/HIPAA compliance and KMS integration to satisfy auditors.

Open technical constraints you asked us to account for:
- No public internet egress from the air-gapped zone (must use a controlled jump host or dedicated transit).
- Allowlist-based firewall changes only; change window lead time ~2 weeks.
- Preference for mutual-TLS + private peering (leased line or customer VPN) over internet VPN if feasible.

Attachments I’m sharing: Redwood SOC evidence summary (high level) and our initial checklist for an on-prem pilot. Please provide Novamed’s sanitized network diagram and a short list of required outbound IPs/ports so Jordan can map connectivity options.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Maya: share a redacted network zones diagram (can redact internal host ranges) — target EOD Thu.
2) Redwood (Jordan + infra): do a technical deep-dive once we have the diagram — propose Tue/Wed next week.
3) Priya/Ben: align commercial path (pilot scope, pricing corridors) after tech sync.

If this aligns, I’ll log the HubSpot tasks and attach the SOC summary to the deal (RW-DEV-5462).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-soc2-evidence-summary.pdf (summary), initial-onprem-checklist.xlsx (referenced)
From: Maya Desai <maya.desai@novamed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: infosec@novamed.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: VPC residency risk map + prioritized asks

Priya —

Thanks for the clear recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications and commitments from our side:

Clarifications:
- The air-gap requirement applies only to the PHI staging and model scoring buckets for our clinical triage pipeline. Non-PHI telemetry can flow to cloud for analytics.
- Residency: primary residency must be US (us-east-1), but we have a small EU subset for EU patients that will need separate handling later.

What we’ll provide:
- Sanitized network zones diagram (novamed-network-zones.pdf attached). We’ll redact internal host ranges but will include DMZ/jump host details and egress controls.
- Point of contact for InfoSec: Rajiv Kumar (rajiv.kumar@novamed.com) — he’ll own the controls review and questionnaire.

Procurement notes:
- We have an internal procurement checkpoint on Nov 3; commercial terms for the pilot should be clear by then to get calendar priority.

Quote from the call: "We can do a controlled peering path but need to validate whether mutual TLS + private peering covers our audit requirement."

I’ll send the sanitized diagram by EOD Thursday and loop Rajiv if we need to set expectations around the questionnaire.

-Maya

Maya / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attached diagram. A few notes from our side and a proposed agenda for the tech deep-dive:

Immediate notes:
- Jordan: please confirm whether Redwood’s on-prem package can be constrained to the customer-resident subnet with no outbound NAT from that zone; also list any artifacts we’ll need for SOC/HIPAA review.
- From a risk perspective we’ll need: KMS integration option (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed), proof points for network segmentation, and an operational runbook for incident response.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60–75 min)
1) Diagram walkthrough and firewall change window implications (Jordan + Novamed network engineer)
2) Connectivity options: private peering vs. dedicated circuit vs. managed VPN (include estimated lead times)
3) Key management and TLS requirements (KMS/HSM, mTLS setup)
4) Pilot scope: throughput targets, acceptance tests, rollback/fallback policy
5) Action log and owner assignments

I’ve attached the Redwood SOC summary to help accelerate the controls conversation. Can we lock a 1-hour slot next Tuesday (Oct 26) between 10:00–12:00 PT? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a brief pre-read.

I’ll also create the HubSpot task and reference RW-DEV-5462.

Thanks,
Ben
